title: [aotautograd] Don't recompute reads of mutated inputs or mutable buffers for auto AC
body:
Summary:
## The issue

The AOT min-cut partitioner decides, per value the backward needs, whether to
save it or to recompute it. Recompute is only equivalent to saving when
re-executing the producing ops yields the same value. That does not hold for a
read of a tensor that is mutated in between.

Recompute defers a read to backward time, and a read of mutable state is a
snapshot:

```
T0  forward:   v  = counts[bin_ids]     # counts == A, this value feeds `where`
T1             counts.index_add_(...)   # counts becomes B
T2  backward:  v' = counts[bin_ids]     # counts == B, so v' != v
```

The input itself is never recomputed -- it is a graph input. What is recomputed
is the intermediate derived from it (`index` -> `gt`), and keeping the input live
into the backward is the consequence of that choice. It looks free to the cost
model, because a buffer already resident costs nothing extra to keep.

Two symptoms follow, and which one you get depends on plumbing the author does
not control:

- **Silently wrong gradients.** When the update moves a value across the
  predicate, the recomputed `cond` disagrees with the one the forward used and
  `torch.where`'s backward routes gradients down the wrong branch.
- **`RuntimeError: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been
  modified by an inplace operation: [...] is at version 1; expected version 0`**,
  when the input reaches the backward through `SavedVariable`, whose version
  counter catches it. That check is a backstop, not the bug.

## Two kinds, and why they need different fixes

**1. Mutated inside this graph.** The in-place update is functionalized into a
`copy_` epilogue, and `fw_metadata.input_info[i].mutates_data` records it. The
hazard is fully visible in the graph being partitioned, so the fix is precise:
mark every reader of such an input `MUST_SAVE`. Marking at the *reader* is what
makes it sufficient -- any backward chain that would touch the input must pass
through a direct reader, so once those are saved the input need not be live in
the backward at all.

The exemption for the in-place chain itself walks only nodes that directly take a
mutated input. It deliberately does not walk the mutation value's transitive
ancestors: the update can depend on arbitrary earlier computation -- dependent
task arches feed into it in the motivating model -- and exempting that whole cone
silently skips genuine readers of the same buffer.

**2. Mutated outside this graph.** A buffer can be read here and updated by a
different compiled region, or by eager code. `input_info` describes only this
region, so it reports nothing, and there is no `copy_` to find: the graph shows
one gather and zero mutations. No analysis of the graph handed to the partitioner
can recover this. So the question changes from "is this mutated?" to "could it
be?", answered from the tensor's kind: buffers hold mutable state by design and
are never recomputed through; parameters are excluded, since the optimizer
updates them between iterations rather than between a forward and its own
backward, and recomputing activations from weights is the main win activation
checkpointing buys.

This half is conservative rather than proven, so it is off by default behind
`ban_recompute_through_buffers`.

## Notes on the implementation

Recovering which inputs are buffers takes a detour: under
`inline_inbuilt_nn_modules` Dynamo hands params and buffers to AOT as ordinary
graph inputs, so `aot_module_simplified`'s `buffers_len` is 0 and every
descriptor is `PlainAOTInput`. The split is recovered from the values -- module
attributes are exactly the static inputs, and those that are not `nn.Parameter`
are buffers.

Effect tokens are prepended to the graph inputs, so a position in `input_info` is
`num_tokens` placeholders further along. Indices are resolved to node names in
`graph_compile`, where that offset is known, rather than handing the partitioner
an index space it has to interpret.

## `activation_memory_budget == 0`

That path early-returned `node_info.inputs` before `solve_min_cut`, which is where
`should_ban_recomputation` consults the tag -- so at maximum recompute both halves
of this change were silently bypassed. It now keeps `MUST_SAVE` forward nodes too.
Recompute is a memory/compute tradeoff; not being value-preserving is a
correctness constraint, and no budget setting should be able to trade it away.

## Known limitation

The parameter exemption assumes parameters are stable between a forward and its
own backward. `_apply_optimizer_in_backward` breaks that assumption and is used
in APS (`aps_models/ads/common/distributed/parallel.py`). Banning recompute
through parameters would gut activation checkpointing, so params stay exempt;
that combination is a pre-existing hazard this diff does not address.

---
🛡️ code-knight prevention: reviewed `unused_vars_params`, `py_length_idioms`, `py_weak_assert`, `py_missing_annotations`, `py_fstring_noph` in *12 files* — deferred for review

Test Plan:
## Unit test

`test_min_cut_partitioner_no_recompute_through_mutated_buffer` in
`caffe2/test/functorch/test_aotdispatch.py` covers both kinds.

*Mutated in this graph*: a buffer read by N gathers and mutated once, the update
sharing bin ids with the last gather only. Later tasks consume earlier ones, so
an earlier gather is an ancestor of the update -- the shape that catches an
over-broad exemption. Asserts the backward does not re-read the buffer, and that
grads match eager.

*Mutated outside this graph*: a buffer this graph only reads, mutated between the
forward and the backward, at `activation_memory_budget=0` so the partitioner
defers every read it is allowed to. Reproduces the production symptom exactly --
without the rule the backward raises

```
RuntimeError: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been
modified by an inplace operation: [torch.DoubleTensor [16]] is at version 1;
expected version 0 instead.
```

and with it enabled the backward does not re-read the buffer and grads match
eager. A smaller budget was tried first and was not enough: at this size the
solver declines the unsafe cut, so the case passed for the wrong reason.

```
buck2 test @//mode/opt fbcode//caffe2/test/functorch:test_aotdispatch \
    -- --regex 'no_recompute_through_mutated_buffer'
  Pass 3. Fail 0.
```

Confirmed non-vacuous: with `force_save_fw_mutated_input_readers` neutered, the
test fails with

```
AssertionError: True is not false : backward re-reads the buffer, ntasks=2
```

## Regression

```
buck2 test @//mode/opt fbcode//caffe2/test/functorch:test_ac_knapsack \
    fbcode//caffe2/test/functorch:test_ac_logging
  Pass 21. Fail 0.

buck2 test @//mode/opt fbcode//caffe2/test/functorch:test_aotdispatch \
    -- --regex '(partition|recompute|memory_budget|min_cut|mutat|cache|effect|token)'
  Pass 219. Fail 1.
```

The one failure is `test_min_cut_partitions_device_valued_node`, which errors with
`CUDA error: device kernel image is invalid`. It fails the same way with this
diff's test file shelved, and the diff is Python-only partitioning logic, so this
is the devvm's GPU not matching the prebuilt CUDA kernels. I did not isolate it
against the parent commit.

## End to end

ig_him (`aps-f1140775701-1140794033`), with the buffer rule enabled. Previous
attempts died inside ~10 minutes on the version-counter error.

```
                                 before        after
  runtime                     ~10 min, crash   5.4 h clean, 0 restarts
  f64[5000] live into bwd     8 -> 2 -> 1      0  (of 91 backward graphs)
  task-arch compile regions   41 (frame 35)    1  (frame 31)
  window_qps                  13,116           ~13,330
```

The task arch is now a single 6,461-line forward graph with the losses,
calibration and label aggregator fused into it, and no graph breaks. The QPS
figure is indicative, not a controlled A/B: different package and day, and it
carries other in-flight changes.
